title: Kingdom of Brycheiniog
capsule: Brycheiniog was an early medieval Welsh kingdom in the upper Usk valley, founded in the fifth century by the Hiberno-Welsh prince Brychan, whose father Anlach secured local power through marriage into a Romano-British family. Centred on Talgarth and the lake-fort at Llangorse (Llyn Syfaddan), it functioned as a buffer between Mercia and Deheubarth, and in the 880s King Elisse submitted to Alfred the Great to secure protection from Viking raids. In 916 Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, stormed Llangorse, capturing the king's wife and thirty-four courtiers. The kingdom's independence ended when the Norman lord Bernard de Neufmarché conquered it between 1088 and 1093, converting it into the Lordship of Brecknock; its name survives in Brecknockshire and the Brecon Beacons (Welsh: Bannau Brycheiniog).
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; the kingdom's boundaries are inferred from later lordship records and hagiographic traditions, with no surviving boundary surveys from the period.
